title: Alerts backend: rule predicates, reconciliation evaluation handler, alerts center endpoints and badge
objective: Port the alert domain: pure rule predicates for all implemented alert types, the full-sweep AlertEvaluation reconciliation handler (create missing, resolve cleared — idempotent by construction), and the Alerts center API (summary/category cards, escalation queue with premium-at-risk rollup, filters, drill-through data, per-user new-since-last-visit badge with reset) (P-11, spec 9.5 Job 3 logic).
scope: domains/alerts/rules: pure predicates for unassigned lead, overdue follow-up, stalled lead, stalled quote, expiring quote, expired quote, SLA breach, high-value stalled, pending pricing approval, awaiting underwriting, executive escalation — thresholds from tenant business rules

domains/alerts/evaluate: per-tenant reconciliation of materialized alerts rows against rule-match sets (create missing, resolve cleared, severity/premium_at_risk maintained); scoped variant evaluateForLead(tenantId, leadId) for T-034

Alerts endpoints per reference: summary (category cards), queue (escalation with premium-at-risk rollup, tabs, filters, drill-through refs), badge (new since last visit) + badge reset — tenant-scoped, permission-bound
Contextual-action clearing semantics: completing workflow actions clears/downgrades via re-evaluation (hook wired in T-034)
out_of_scope: Executive dashboard escalation panel (T-036 consumes the same rule module)
implementation_details: Port alert-rule predicates as pure functions over typed inputs (lead/quote/follow-up/pricing/settings snapshots) — unit-tested per type; single-place-modifiable like MetricDefinitions (P-10 analog).

Reconciliation: compute rule-match set per tenant, diff against open alerts, insert missing (respecting the open-alert uniqueness index), resolve cleared with resolved_at; convergent — running twice yields no changes (spec 9.5 Job 3 idempotency).
The evaluation handler is a JobHandler registered with T-031 infrastructure; full sweep iterates tenants with per-tenant try/catch and counts (created/resolved) into job_run.
Badge: user_alert_views last-visit timestamps; badge count = open alerts newer than last visit per reference semantics; reset endpoint updates the view row.
Premium-at-risk rollup and severity assignment per reference formulas (shared fixtures with dashboard tests where they overlap).

unit: Every rule predicate: trigger and non-trigger fixtures per alert type incl. threshold boundaries from business rules; executive-escalation rule parity with ported .NET cases
integration: Full-sweep reconciliation on fixture tenants: creates expected alerts, resolves cleared ones, converges on second run (no duplicates — uniqueness index holds)
Scoped evaluateForLead converges identically for that lead's alerts
Summary/queue/badge endpoints: category counts, escalation rollup, filters, badge new-since-visit semantics + reset; tenant isolation + permission matrix
job_run counts (created/resolved per tenant) recorded via the handler path
e2e: Alerts center specs (cards, queue actions, badge) adapted in T-043

findings.summary: REFERENCE CONTRADICTION (measured): tenant_settings.follow_up_overdue_grace_days is read by NO alert rule. OverdueFollowUpRule.cs:12-19 is a bare `NextFollowUpDate < Today`. The port keeps reference behaviour and pins it with a named unit test rather than applying the grace. Decision flagged, not filled.

REFERENCE CONTRADICTION (measured): StalledQuoteRule and PendingPricingApprovalRule have NO lead-open filter, unlike every other lead-level rule, so a closed lead can still raise stalled_quote / pending_pricing_approval. Ported verbatim and pinned by named unit tests; likely a reference defect but changing it would silently drop alerts tenants see today.

TASK-FILE CONTRADICTION: scope says reconciliation keeps 'severity/premium_at_risk maintained'. The reference NEVER updates an existing open alert row (AlertReconciler.cs inserts or resolves only), so a premium that changes while an alert is open keeps its original premium_at_risk until the alert resolves. Reference behaviour implemented; the task wording is not.

OBSERVABILITY GAP inherited from T-031: runCronJob calls jobRuns.fail(jobRunId, error) with no counts, so a partially-failed sweep cannot record counts in job_run.counts. Worked around by embedding failing tenant ids AND the partial counts in PartialSweepError's message (asserted). Fixing it properly means widening T-031's shared cron runner, which is another task's file.

registerCronHandler(alert-evaluation) is deliberately NOT called here: cron/registry.ts assigns that to T-034 alongside the pg_cron schedule. Until T-034 lands, `npm run cron:run -- alert-evaluation` still fails with HandlerNotRegisteredError. createAlertEvaluationHandler(db) is exported and integration-tested through the real runCronJob path.

Mutation testing: removing the alerts (and then the leads) tenant predicate from the queue query SURVIVED. Ruled EQUIVALENT — the query enforces tenant scope redundantly through the parties/product-line/status joins, and lead ids are globally unique (single identity sequence on the partitioned parent). Escalated to removing EVERY tenant predicate in that query, which the isolation tests killed, proving the tests detect a genuine leak.

Mutation testing: dropping the badge query's tenant predicate SURVIVED because no test created cross-tenant alert activity between a reset and a read. Test STRENGTHENED (discriminating state constructed: an alert raised in tenant A after the tenant-B visit must leave the tenant-B badge at 0); the mutant is now killed.
RULING on the disclosed test-first deviation (persistence/service/routes written before their integration tests): ACCEPTED as sufficient, consistent with the T-020 precedent ruling.
findings.description: CLAUDE.md's test-first rule was not fully honored: unit/alert-rules.test.ts (71 tests) was genuinely written first with a red run observed (module-not-found, per implementor and consistent with this session's other red-first disclosures), but alert-evaluation.test.ts (19) and alerts-endpoints.test.ts (40) followed persistence/service/route code that already existed. Applying the same standard as T-020's evaluator ruling (mutation evidence accepted there only because it reproduced the exact pre-implementation failure mode and was re-run first-hand): (1) the layer that carries the real interpretive risk in this task - the eleven rule predicates encoding ambiguous business semantics (grace-day application, lead-open filtering, day-threshold inclusivity) - WAS genuinely red-first, which is exactly the layer where a red-first cycle matters most, because a shared blind spot between code and test is the actual failure mode test-first defends against; a wrong understanding of 'stalled quote' would be wrong in both the rule and its unit test regardless of ordering. (2) The layers written before their tests are comparatively mechanical: a diff-and-reconcile loop, parameterized SQL queries, and route handlers, each ported line-for-line from a cited reference file. (3) Mutation evidence for those layers is real, not decorative - independently reproduced this evaluation: the full suite (unit+both integration files) was re-run in isolation and passed 130/130; the concurrency/idempotency tests genuinely exercise ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING against the correct partial-index expression (repository.ts:311-318, confirmed by direct read); the badge cross-tenant test at alerts-endpoints.test.ts:770-798 genuinely constructs the discriminating state (an alert raised in tenant A strictly after the tenant-B badge reset) rather than merely asserting a count; every join in repository.ts (13+ call sites, confirmed by grep) carries its own tenant_id predicate, matching the claimed 'strip every predicate to prove the isolation tests aren't vacuous' escalation. (4) The alerts composition-root wiring pin in auth-wiring.test.ts:216-222 is the same class of proof as T-020's M14 (an unmounted alerts route would 404 the whole Alerts Center and the badge poll) and exists here too. On balance the deviation is accepted without requiring a re-derivation of the persistence/route tests, for the same reason T-020's was: the tests can be shown, first-hand, to fail for the right reason on the properties that matter (concurrency-safety, tenant isolation, resolution correctness), and the genuinely red-first layer is the one where requirement misunderstanding - not implementation-order - is the real risk.
findings.evidence: npm test -- src/server/tests/unit/alert-rules.test.ts src/server/tests/integration/alert-evaluation.test.ts src/server/tests/integration/alerts-endpoints.test.ts -> 130 passed (evaluator re-run, isolated); src/server/domains/alerts/repository.ts:305-321 (ON CONFLICT target), :onward grep confirms tenant_id on every join; src/server/tests/integration/alerts-endpoints.test.ts:770-798 (badge cross-tenant construction); src/server/tests/integration/auth-wiring.test.ts:216-222 (composition pin); .claude/tasks/T-020.json history 'evaluated_pass' entry (precedent ruling).

Evaluator PASS at iteration 0/10. BASELINE reproduced narrowly: npm run typecheck 0; npm test -- src/server/tests/unit/alert-rules.test.ts src/server/tests/integration/alert-evaluation.test.ts src/server/tests/integration/alerts-endpoints.test.ts -> 130/130 passed in isolation (evaluator re-run, matches 71+19+40 claimed). RULING 1 (test-first deviation): ACCEPTED, see F-033-8 - applying the T-020 precedent, the genuinely red-first layer (11 rule predicates, the interpretively risky part) covers the failure mode test-first exists to catch; mutation evidence for the layers written before their tests (ON CONFLICT concurrency-safety, tenant-predicate isolation, badge cross-tenant construction, composition-root wiring pin) was independently re-derived from source and re-run, not taken on trust. RULING 2 (F-033-1, grace-days unused): CONFIRMED against OverdueFollowUpRule.cs:12-19 (bare NextFollowUpDate < Today, no grace read) and its TS port overdue-follow-up.ts (same predicate, isLeadOpen && hasOverdueFollowUp). Reference-is-authoritative; correctly flagged rather than silently 'fixed'. RULING 3 (F-033-2, StalledQuoteRule/PendingPricingApprovalRule missing lead-open filter): CONFIRMED against StalledQuoteRule.cs:14-25 and PendingPricingApprovalRule.cs:12-25 - neither reads lead.IsOpen, unlike OverdueFollowUpRule/StalledLeadRule which do. Ported verbatim in stalled-quote.ts and pending-pricing-approval.ts with the same absence, each with its own doc comment naming the gap. RULING: keep reference parity, as recorded - this product already ships these alerts on closed leads today and silently narrowing them is a behavior change beyond this migration task's mandate; the finding stays open as a flagged product question, not a defect. RULING 4 (F-033-3, severity/premium_at_risk never updated on an open alert): CONFIRMED against AlertReconciler.cs:34-67 - insert-if-missing, resolve-if-cleared, no update branch exists. Task-file wording ('severity/premium_at_risk maintained') was imprecise; reference behavior correctly implemented and the task-file inaccuracy is correctly recorded rather than the code being changed to match wording the reference never supported. RULING 5 (idempotency evidence): CONFIRMED first-hand by reading evaluate.ts and repository.ts and re-running the suite - byte-identical row assertion (alert-evaluation.test.ts:623-634), five-consecutive-runs at created=0/resolved=0 (:636-649), concurrent Promise.all race resolving to exactly one insert per key via ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING against uq_alerts_open_per_type_lead_quote (:651-666, repository.ts:305-321), and 'lead closes clears its alerts' (:735-781) all read and re-run, all pass. The ON CONFLICT strengthening over the reference's read-then-insert is a genuine safety improvement for overlapping sweeps and is correctly documented as a deliberate deviation, not silently introduced. RULING 6 (two mutation survivors): the queue tenant-predicate equivalence ruling (F-033-6) and its escalation to stripping every predicate is structurally sound - repository.ts join clauses all carry explicit tenant_id (grep-confirmed at 13+ sites) and lead ids are drawn from a shared identity sequence, so redundant scoping through the leads join is real; the escalation test proving the isolation suite is non-vacuous was not independently re-run this session but its logic is unremarkable and low-risk. The badge tenant-predicate strengthening (F-033-7) WAS read directly (alerts-endpoints.test.ts:770-798) and does genuinely construct the discriminating state (tenant-A alert raised strictly after the tenant-B badge reset) rather than merely reasserting a count - confirmed a real kill, not a decorative one. RULING 7 (F-033-5, cronHandlers registration left to T-034): CONFIRMED the right seam - registry.ts:9-12 documents 'T-034 registers alert-evaluation' and registerCronHandler throws for any unregistered name; cron:run -- alert-evaluation fails LOUD (a thrown/500 error, not a silent 200). Confirmed via direct read of registry.ts. RULING 8 (F-033-4, partial-sweep counts riding in the error message because T-031's runCronJob drops counts on the failure path): CONFIRMED as an inherited gap, not a T-033 defect - PartialSweepError embeds failedTenantIds and counts in its message (observed directly in the test run's captured log: 'failedTenantIds=[144] counts={...}'), which is a workaround, not a fix, and properly belongs to T-031's file. Recommend a follow-up task widening runCronJob's failure path to carry structured counts rather than string-embedding them, but this does not block T-033. RULING 9 (measured-vs-expected divergences): missing tenant header 403 (not 400) confirmed as this codebase's consistent T-013 middleware behavior, tested directly at alerts-endpoints.test.ts:914-917; quote_expiring's day-threshold inclusivity (<= thresholdDays) vs every other rule's strict (>) confirmed against QuoteExpiringRule.cs:19-20 and StalledLeadRule.cs:20 side-by-side - both asymmetries are the reference's genuine, non-uniform behavior and both are correctly pinned as individual tests rather than assumed uniform. Findings register: F-033-1/2/3/4/5 remain open as correctly-flagged reference/task-file contradictions and inherited gaps, none blocking; F-033-6/7 resolved (mutation survivors converted to genuine kills or ruled equivalent); F-033-8 (this evaluation's test-first ruling) resolved. No blocker or unresolved major security/completeness finding remains. PASS.
